follow100Note: The striking thing: interest alone eats $23.11 of every $100 — four times the $5.66 of operating profit the business itself makes. And this table doesn't even show the capex: the company spent another $257.85 per $100 of revenue buying property and equipment this quarter — funded by debt, customer prepayments, and new shares, not by the business's own cash.

oneTimers: No one-time charges were called out this quarter. The gap between the $709M GAAP net loss and the $529M adjusted net loss is the usual recurring set: $160M of stock-based compensation and $12M of amortization of acquired intangibles, plus $11M of other adjustments (mostly investment gains) and a $19M tax effect.

The tax swing: this quarter carried an $83M tax expense despite a pre-tax loss, versus a $127M tax benefit a year ago — a $210M year-over-year swing that accounts for about a third of why the net loss widened by $599M.
otherDetail: Net non-operating expense of $833M: interest expense, net was $846M — the cost of borrowing heavily to build data centers — partly offset by $13M of other income, net. There was no fair-value gain or loss this quarter.

segments.name: AI cloud infrastructure
segments.note: Renting out GPU-powered cloud capacity purpose-built for AI training and inference (running trained models); the company's single revenue line, up 168% YoY as demand from AI labs, hyperscalers and enterprises surged.

takeaways.text: Revenue hit $3,661M, up from $1,365M a year ago and up more than $1B sequentially, with a $132.5B backlog and guidance raised across the board. Demand for AI computing is not the constraint.
takeaways.title: Growth is real and enormous — revenue nearly tripled

takeaways.text: Operating income quadrupled to $207M, but $846M of quarterly interest — on $46.9B of debt, more than double the $21.4B at year-end 2025 — turns it into a $709M net loss. Every quarter's growth is bought with more borrowing.
takeaways.title: The debt is the whole story underneath

takeaways.text: Operating cash flow was a healthy $1,975M, but capex of $9,441M means $7.5B of free-cash burn in one quarter — covered by $4.2B of convertible notes, new debt facilities, and ~$9B of customer prepayments expected in the next three months. The model works as long as customers keep prepaying and lenders keep lending.
takeaways.title: The cash burn is funded, for now

verdict: CoreWeave's revenue nearly tripled to a record $3.66 billion and operating profit quadrupled, but the company still lost $709 million because $846 million of interest on its $47 billion debt pile swallowed the entire operating profit — and it is spending $9.4 billion a quarter on new data centers to keep growing.
